target_customer: Nuclear medicine, industrial, research and defense buyers of radioisotopes
problem: Most Mo-99 comes from a few aging government reactors abroad. Atomic Alchemy aimed to build private reactors dedicated to isotope production in the US.

founders.name: Thomas Eiden
education: University of Wisconsin-Madison (nuclear fuels research, degree not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC bio: former reactor engineer and core designer at the Advanced Test Reactor.

competitors.name: NorthStar Medical Radioisotopes
competitors.what: Accelerator based Mo-99 production in Beloit, Wisconsin
competitors.traction_then: Broke ground on its facility per Physics Today November 2019

competitors.name: SHINE
competitors.what: Fusion neutron based Mo-99 and other isotope production
competitors.traction_then: Planned production per Physics Today November 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing and licensing a private reactor for isotopes needs nuclear engineering and NRC approval, beyond a normal software team.

defensibility.rationale: Reactor licensing and capital requirements deter copycats, though NorthStar and SHINE pursued the same market.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Oklo agreed to buy it in an all-stock deal valued at 25M announced Nov 2024 and closed in early 2025, keeping the Atomic Alchemy brand.

market_need_then: YC page notes Mo-99 supply depends on a few aging government reactors abroad. Physics Today in 2019 describes several competitors racing to supply it.

brand_strength.rationale: Evocative name with a registered word mark filed March 2020, and Oklo kept it as a subsidiary brand, but no press or community about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Atomic Alchemy, founded by a former Advanced Test Reactor engineer, sought to build private isotope reactors. It stayed small in disclosed funding and was acquired by Oklo for a reported 25M in stock after a November 2024 letter of intent, becoming a subsidiary. The sale looks like a strategic fit for Oklo's isotope plans rather than a scaled standalone business.
notes: Business Wire page returned 403, deal terms come from search result summaries. Closing date varies: Feb 28 2025 in some sources, March 2025 on YC page. PitchBook lists 28.4M for the deal. Funding aggregators conflict (CB Insights 650K, PitchBook 150K accelerator and 150K seed) and are not recorded as rounds. Oklo is listed as investor by CB Insights, unconfirmed. Completeness pass: searches found no dated round; CB Insights (650K) and PitchBook (150K) conflict and give no dates, so none recorded. Oklo's USD 25M all-stock acquisition is the exit, not a round.
